reviews.reason: C1932 measures a floor of 77.75%, which falls outside the first-pass '80-98%' (the first pass's own 79% already did), and quotes the chart's 'not a defective-code percentage' framing. C2078 adds the author's own staleness caveat. C2031's Oxlint catalogue is anecdotal and would add a third-party tool on top of ESLint, so it opens nothing.

C1934 and C2079 restate the first-pass callable and complexity figures (Fable 8,967/3.57, SOL6 Medium 1,083/11.70). C1923 restates the gaming caveat. C2077 shows slop coverage failing to predict strict passes, which strengthens the 'no single metric gates' reading. No card brings evidence of a new kind.

C2081 is Dex endorsing metric backpressure on the strength of a co-host's BAML experiment, with no numbers reported. By that relayed account the guidelines did not improve worst-function complexity, the cc_max dimension a gate would rest on. C1934 and C2079 repeat the gameability finding that sank the first pass.

C1933 adds measured final SLOC volume (about 9x spread across campaigns). That is consistent with degradation but is another benchmark statistic. It does not change the transfer argument, and the F017 audit trial still covers the actionable part.

C2039 measures benchmark scores (about 16.5%), not the benchmark design's value to this repo. C2166 describes a benchmark still being built, with no results. Building a benchmark remains out of scope for a one-developer product repo.

C1911, C1926 and C1929 restate the first-pass figures with more detail: 10 campaigns spanning $178.51-$1,550.07 inside a 12.24-16.33% strict band, no repeated seeds, and 2 of 3 pairs losing passes at xhigh. C2066 'contradicts' is a spoken reading of a chart that gave no numbers. It conflicts with C1926's GPT-6 SOL 30-to-26 drop, so it does not outweigh the measured pairs. The claim stays background for the G4-F034 trial.

C1911 is tagged 'contradicts', but it measures strict passes against cost, while this family's counter-datum is about open defects against cost. It does not test the claim, which stays a small caveat that keeps G4-F034 a trial.

C1914, C1932 and C2077 restate the first-pass 77.75% vs 94.25% figure on 28 matched problems, with one run per setting. C1915 confirms that the '~5x cleaner' headline is loose, as the first pass already noted. C2078 says the slop linters are stale, which weakens the cleanliness side of the trade-off. The harness's xhigh verifiers judge claims and do not write code, so the first-pass reason stands.

C2070 gives the benchmark's size and is internally inconsistent (30 vs 36 problems). C2166 describes a benchmark still in progress, with no results. Neither turns the wished-for benchmark into something this repo should build.
